Comet rendering — a SF_KINDS.COMET body is a dark irregular nucleus wrapped in a sublimated gas/dust envelope (coma) trailing two tails. The ion tail is a long narrow streak pointing straight anti-sunward (the solar wind entrains plasma along field lines); the dust tail is shorter, wider and lags the radius vector because grains keep some orbital momentum — it tilts off the anti-sunward line and fans out. Both tails are PARTICLE STREAMS rooted at the nucleus — THREE.Points clouds of soft-glow grains, never quads — whose length and opacity scale with heliocentric proximity: sublimation scales steeply with solar flux, so the tail ignites at periapsis and dies on the outbound leg. Lengths are multiples of the nucleus radius (Halley ≈ 0.2 units → ~6.4-unit ion stream), so the proportions read correctly at chart scale where an honest ~10⁸-km tail would cross the whole map.
